job_spec: High-throughput distributed caching and rate limiting at scale.
question_asked: You need to shard an in-memory rate-limiter cluster while minimizing key movement when adding nodes. Which strategy is optimal?
options_text:
- A: Modulo hashing (hash(key) % N) across server indices
- B: Consistent hashing ring with virtual nodes
- C: Store all counters in a single unsharded primary SQL table with row locks
- D: Round-robin counter writes across random cache nodes
user_answer: Virtual nodes keep key redistribution proportional (~1/N) during scaling instead of rehashing most keys.
human_rationale: Candidate selected optimal Option B with sound rationale; should score 95-100 and state Option B is Correct.
